theme: Sunday sugo season: a pork-and-fennel ragù and an olive-oil squash-and-bean traybake to carry a full-house week.

components.name: Pork & Fennel Ragù (the Sunday sugo)
components.ingredients: 2 lb ground pork, 1 lb ground beef, 1 fennel bulb, 2 onions, 3 carrots, 4 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 cup white wine, two 28-oz cans whole tomatoes, fennel seed, bay, Parmigiano rind, olive oil
components.method: Build a slow soffritto: finely dice fennel, onion, and carrot and sweat them in a generous pour of olive oil until soft and sweet, 12-15 min. Push aside and brown the pork and beef hard, undisturbed, to build fond. Toast a spoon of fennel seed and the tomato paste for a minute, then deglaze with the white wine and scrape up the brown bits. Add crushed tomatoes, a parm rind, and bay; simmer gently 90 min until glossy and thick. Cool. Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes beautifully.

components.name: Olive-Oil Roasted Delicata & White Beans
components.ingredients: 3 delicata squash, two 15-oz cans cannellini (drained), 2 pints cherry tomatoes, 5 smashed garlic cloves, rosemary & thyme, chili flakes, lemon, lots of olive oil
components.method: Halve and seed the delicata and cut into skin-on half-moons. On a sheet pan, toss with the drained beans, cherry tomatoes, smashed garlic, herb sprigs, salt, a pinch of chili, and a real flood of olive oil. Roast at 425F for 30-35 min until the squash caramelizes and the tomatoes burst into the oil. Finish with lemon zest. Holds 4-5 days; the tomatoey oil doubles as a dressing.

dinners.name: Rigatoni al Ragù
dinners.ingredients: Pork & fennel ragù, rigatoni, Parmigiano, basil, olive oil
steps: Boil rigatoni in well-salted water until just shy of al dente; save a mug of pasta water.
Warm a big ladle of ragù per portion in a wide pan.
Drain pasta and toss into the ragù with a splash of pasta water, finishing the cook in the sauce.
Off heat, stir in grated parm and a thread of olive oil until glossy; tear basil over.
Serve with more parm at the table.

dinners.name: Baked Polenta with Ragù & Mozzarella
dinners.ingredients: Polenta/coarse cornmeal, pork & fennel ragù, fresh mozzarella, butter, Parmigiano
steps: Cook polenta in salted water, whisking, until creamy; beat in butter and a handful of parm.
Spread half the polenta in a baking dish, spoon over ragù, then the rest of the polenta.
Top with torn fresh mozzarella and a dusting of parm.
Bake at 425F for 15-18 min until bubbling and browned in spots.
Rest 5 min before scooping so it sets up.

dinners.name: White Bean & Squash Soup with Greens
dinners.ingredients: Roasted delicata & white beans, chicken or veg broth, kale or cavolo nero, garlic, lemon, olive oil
steps: Sizzle a little sliced garlic in olive oil in a pot until fragrant.
Add most of the roasted squash-and-bean traybake plus broth to cover; simmer 10 min.
Blend a third of it smooth and stir back for body, leaving the rest chunky.
Fold in shredded kale and cook until tender, 5 min; brighten with lemon.
Ladle into bowls and finish each with a heavy drizzle of olive oil.

dinners.name: Crisp-Seared Cod over Squash & Beans, Salsa Verde
dinners.ingredients: Cod fillets, roasted delicata & white beans, parsley, capers, anchovy, garlic, red wine vinegar, olive oil
steps: Chop a quick salsa verde: parsley, capers, anchovy, garlic, vinegar, and olive oil.
Pat the cod bone-dry and salt it; warm the squash-and-bean traybake in a low oven.
Sear the cod in a hot oiled pan, pressing gently, until a deep golden crust forms; flip once and finish.
Spoon the warm squash and beans onto plates.
Lay the cod on top and spoon salsa verde generously over.

technique.name: Pan-searing white fish for a crisp, golden crust
technique.tiedTo: The seared cod over squash and beans: dry the fillets thoroughly, salt just before cooking, get the pan and oil properly hot, lay the fish down away from you, and DON'T move it until it releases on its own. Press lightly for full contact and flip only once. That patience is the whole difference between steamed-grey and crusted-golden.

shopping.items: 1 fennel bulb, 3 onions, 3 carrots, 2 heads garlic, 3 delicata squash, 2 pints cherry tomatoes, 2 lemons, bunch kale or cavolo nero, basil, parsley, rosemary, thyme
2 lb ground pork, 1 lb ground beef, 6 cod fillets (~2 lb)
fresh mozzarella, Parmigiano-Reggiano wedge (with rind), butter

two 28-oz cans whole tomatoes, two 15-oz cans cannellini, tomato paste, polenta/coarse cornmeal, rigatoni, white wine, red wine vinegar, anchovies, capers, fennel seed, bay, chili flakes, olive oil, chicken or veg broth

scaleNote: Girls are home this week, so everything above is already sized for 6 (2 adults + 4 girls under 10). Kid tweaks: keep chili flakes on the side rather than in the traybake, cut the delicata into smaller coins, and pull a little plain buttered rigatoni for any picky eater before saucing. The ragù batch easily covers both the rigatoni and the baked-polenta night with some to freeze. For the 2-adult weeks (next handoff to Jen is ~Oct 4), halve the ragù or freeze half, drop to one can of beans and 2 delicata, cook 2-3 cod fillets, and lean the fish and soup nights harder into technique.
